prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in this moire platform

statement.case_for: I keep magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene as my preferred single-part prize after the full first-round exchange. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gave a quantitative, falsifiable prediction of flat bands at a magic angle from a simple starting point, and the 2018 transport experiments showed that a single tunable device realises correlated insulators and superconductivity. Many independent groups have since reproduced and extended this with transport, tunnelling and scanning-probe spectroscopy, and the field now includes other moire systems and tunable Chern bands. In my own area, this is where first-principles band theory and many-body theory meet a controllable experiment, and the structure of prediction followed by realisation is the one I weigh most. I have narrowed the citation in response to Danielsson: it rewards the prediction of the flat bands and the observation of the phenomena and makes no claim on the pairing mechanism. The chair's question is whether the open mechanism and the credit gap outweigh the breadth. For me the breadth still wins, but not by a large margin.
statement.case_against: The reservations are real and I do not think they are small. The superconducting pairing mechanism is unresolved and twist-angle disorder complicates what is intrinsic. Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 experiments, cannot be named from the supplied credited names, and earlier twisted-bilayer band theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) and other moire experiments (Dean, Young, Yazdani) also have claims. Six of eight members, including several who regard the physics as excellent, judge that these points favour optical lattice clocks (B007), which have a compact two-name attribution, a reproduced 1e-18 result and a distinct invention in magic-wavelength trapping. B007 does face the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes and a redefinition of the second that has not yet happened. I would not regard B007 as a wrong prize, and I would accept it if the committee decides that attribution and maturity should decide the matter.

responses.point: Kroll prefers B007 for Katori and Ye as an original discovery-by-instrument with the most compact attribution on the list, and treats B005 as early because the interpretation of the superconductivity is not stable.
responses.response: I accept his central point that B007 has an unambiguous measurable outcome and the cleaner credit chain, and I accept that the mechanism is open. I do not accept that this makes B005 premature. The flat-band prediction, the correlated insulators and the superconducting domes are phenomena that have been reproduced, and a citation can be limited to them. High-temperature superconductivity was recognised in 1987 without an agreed mechanism. His point that Ye's contribution extends beyond the first lattice clock to many-body clock physics does strengthen the two-name case for B007, and I record that it moves me a little. I do not move my preferred configuration because of it.

responses.point: Lindroth keeps B007 first as an original, clean and widely confirmed idea, but notes that precision metrology has been honoured repeatedly in 1997, 2005 and 2012, and says B005 would be easier to defend in a few years.
responses.response: She states the overlap concern with B007 more candidly than I did in round 1, and I think it is the main weakness of the clock case: the committee has to show that the neutral-atom magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct achievement and not another step in a recognised lineage. Her view that B005 can wait is the thing I most disagree with. A prize that waits for the mechanism to be settled would leave out phenomena that are already well established, and eight years of replication is not early by the standard we have applied before. I agree with her, though, that the clock concept itself is separable from the comb and ion prizes if the citation is worded around neutral-atom lattice trapping.

responses.point: Mehlig moved from B025 to B007, citing the sharp magic-wavelength concept and the clean two-person split, and in round 1 told me that a prize for the moire platform is easier to defend a few years from now than a prize for an interpretation not yet settled.
responses.response: I take his point that the prediction of the flat bands is the more secure part of the B005 case, and the citation I now propose rests on it. I disagree that the committee is being asked to award an interpretation. We would be awarding a prediction and an observation, and the interpretation question belongs to the future literature. On the credit side he is right that Bistritzer's share relative to MacDonald is a legitimate question, but the 2011 prediction was a joint paper with the explicit magic-angle calculation, and I do not see a principled way to separate the two.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, ranks B007 first, says the credit list for B005 admits real disputes that B007 does not, and says B007 is the natural runner-up rather than a wrong choice if the committee judges twisted bilayer graphene the larger discovery.
responses.response: I agree that the asymmetry in attribution is real and I flagged it myself, so I will not argue that it is imaginary. I would add that a three-name limit leaves out someone in nearly every collaborative discovery, and that it should not decide between a prize for an instrument and a prize for a new platform. His remark that B007 is the natural runner-up if the committee prefers B005 is also how I see it from the other side, which is why B007 is my first alternative. I also accept his point that I should be challenged on my field proximity, and I have kept my conflict note below.

responses.point: Danielsson also prefers B005 with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer, but would keep the citation to the prediction and observation of the phenomena and avoid any wording that implies a settled explanation of the pairing.
responses.response: I adopt this wording and have narrowed my citation accordingly. I note that the two of us moved to B005 for different reasons, which weakens any argument that the B005 minority is one bloc: he sees breadth across the openings, while I weigh prediction followed by realisation. His three-name argument, that the prediction is a joint result and the model's authorship is not separable, matches my own.

uncertainties: Whether the open pairing mechanism and the twist-angle disorder make B005 premature, or whether the reproduced phenomenology is enough for a prize.
How to handle the omission of Yuan Cao and the earlier twisted-bilayer theory, and whether Jarillo-Herrero alone is the right experimental credit.
Whether the neutral-atom magic-wavelength lattice clock is distinct enough from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and whether the claimed impact on the redefinition of the second is realised.
Whether the committee will weigh clean attribution above the breadth of a new platform, which is a judgement not settled by the support counts.
I rely on recalled priority history rather than verified records, particularly for the 2011 and 2018 papers.
statement.conflict_note: No specific personal or institutional conflict is apparent from my profile for MacDonald, Bistritzer, Jarillo-Herrero, Katori or Ye. My field proximity is the relevant disclosure: I work on first-principles and many-body electronic-structure theory and on two-dimensional materials, which could bias me toward moire quantum matter and toward theory-plus-experiment prizes in correlated electrons. The chair's summary records this, and I ask that my preference be weighed with it in mind.
